is kristen colson and i'm a quality programs manager for the american heart association before we begin i'd like to quickly review how to use this platform for today's event if you would like a copy feedback survey this presentation will be recorded and available within the coming weeks at heart org forward slash painmanagement it is my pleasure to introduce our speaker for today dr robert carey dr carey is dean emeritus and professor of medicine at the university of virginia school of medicine his research on hormonal control of blood pressure and hypertension has resulted in over 450 publications and has been funded continuously by the national institutes of health since 1973 dr carey co chaired the 2017 american college of cardiology american heart association high blood pressure guideline writing committee and chaired the aha scientific writing committee on resistant hypertension he has received numerous awards including the distinguished physician and the outstanding leadership awards of the endocrine society the aha excellence award for hypertension research the aha distinguished scientist award and election to the american society for clinical investigation the association of american physicians and the national academy of medicine dr carey the floor is yours well thank you kristen i'm delighted to be able to give this webinar on guideline driven management of hypertension this will be an evidence based review my disclosures are here of mainly membership on writing committees of various kinds the outline of today's presentation will begin with a brief review of major guideline recommendations and then talk about optimal systolic blood pressure and primordial disease prevention followed by some information on the current state of blood pressure control we will talk about two kinds of secondary hypertension that induced by drugs that people take and the other primary aldosteronism in which there's recent updated literature we will then focus on the treatment of hypertension in young adults at low short term cardiovascular disease risk and then cover lifestyle management and pharmacologic management of hypertension and then particularly focus on blood pressure management of older adults and then we'll conclude with some summary comments i intend to structure this as a series of issues and questions we'll first review the major guideline recommendations and this slide on the left shows systolic and diastolic blood pressures in the blood pressure classifications of the jnc 7 guideline published in 2003 and the 2017 american college of physicians and american heart association guideline published in 2017 and for these guidelines normal blood pressure was unchanged from the 2003 jnc 7 to the 2017 acc aha guideline but there was a large change in this broad area pre hypertension which in the jnc 7 report went from 120 over 80 to 139 over 89 and we broke that into two categories elevated blood pressure and stage one hypertension because there was an increasing risk of cardiovascular events occurring as one stepped up from normal to elevated blood pressure to stage one hypertension so stage one hypertension currently is 130 139 over 80 to 89 we then made stage two hypertension the previous stage one hypertension and that's anything over 140 over 90 and we did not have any additional stages in the 2017 guideline of importance blood pressure to be classified into one of these categories needs to be based on an average of at least two careful readings on at least two occasions and if the systolic or diastolic blood pressure is different in the two categories the individual should be designated as the higher blood pressure category and this slide shows the thresholds in the 2017 guideline for drug treatment and of course we didn't recommend any drug treatment for those with normal or elevated blood pressure just healthy lifestyle non pharmacologic therapy for stage one hypertension which is 130 to 139 over 80 to 89 the threshold was based on cardiovascular disease risk and the presence or absence of cardiovascular disease if there was no cardiovascular disease or a very low 10 year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk ascvd risk of less than 10 then non pharmacologic therapy was recommended but if there was cvd or a high ascvd risk then antihypertensive drug therapy was recommended to be added to non pharmacologic therapy and the patients with diabetes or chronic kidney disease since they are at much higher risk than others were automatically placed in high risk category and requiring antihypertensive drug therapy to begin with for those age greater than 65 years the blood pressure category of 130 to 139 antihypertensive drug therapy was also recommended because older people like diabetics and patients with ckd have high cardiovascular risk and of course for stage two hypertension which is greater than 140 over 90 irrespective of the cardiovascular risk these patients should be treated with antihypertensive drug therapy at least one if not two drugs to begin with this slide shows the antihypertensive treatment targets for the 2017 guideline and of course there are no treatment targets until you get into treatment with antihypertensive drugs in which case whether you have a high ascvd risk or presence of cvd or diabetes or ckd you should aim for a target systolic blood pressure of less than 130 diastolic blood pressure of less than 80 if you are in the older age category greater than or equal to 65 and your blood pressure is greater than or equal to 130 the target is less than 130 systolic now having reviewed the classification of blood pressure in terms of thresholds and goals there was a controversy surrounding the 2017 guideline recommendations when they initially appeared have the major guideline recommendations been validated there are two reports the first one is a comparison of cvd events and death prevented with adherence to two guideline recommendations the 2014 evidence based panel report which had higher thresholds and goals of treatment than the 2017 guideline which had lower thresholds and goals so again the threshold for initiation of antihypertensive therapy in the 2017 guideline was blood pressure greater than 140 over 90 for the general population with low ascvd risk and if you had high risk it was greater than or equal to 130 over 80 and then the goal as you saw was less than 130 over 80 as compared to less than 140 90 or 150 over 90 depending on their age in the 2014 report now if you compare the cvd events that were prevented by adherence to these two guidelines there were 270,000 in the 2014 evidence based guideline as opposed to 610,000 in the 2017 guideline and the annual reduction in death paralleled that at 177,000 for the 2014 report as compared to 334,000 for the 2017 accaha guideline the second report was a simulated population impact of achieving and maintaining the 2017 blood pressure goals in adults greater than or equal to 45 years of age with hypertension compared to maintaining current blood pressure treatment and control goals or achieving blood pressure goals recommended in the jnc report of 2003 or compared with the 2017 8 th jnc panel report on blood pressure goals and the estimates were made by using a population called regards weighted to the u s population they used the national health and nutrition survey for estimating the u s population and used a meta analysis published by josh bundy it's a beautiful network meta analysis on the cvd risk reduction with blood pressure lowering they also estimated the serious adverse events with blood pressure lowering based on pool data from the sprint and accord large clinical trials and this analysis showed that the 2017 guideline prevented 3 million cardiovascular disease events the jnc 7 2.6 million and the jnc 8 panel report down to 1.6 million events prevented so two well performed simulation studies demonstrate a highly positive population impact following the 2017 guideline recommendations for lowering blood pressure in hypertensive persons compared to other guidelines the increased risk of adverse events which are largely reversible with lower blood pressure targets should not be equated to the risk reduction of major clinical events significant reduction in all cause mortality shows that the benefits of treatment truly outweigh the risks and these reductions or these results strongly support a lower blood pressure target less than 130 over 80 in the management of hypertension so given those reports is there any association of blood pressure levels within the normal intensive range with cardiovascular events or disease and what do the data say about the importance of primordial prevention well what is primordial prevention anyway well that is actions that inhibit the emergence of risk factors that form in the form of environmental economic social and behavioral conditions and cultural patterns of living but the key is prevention of the emergence of risk factors like high blood pressure so the 2017 guideline lowered the systolic blood pressure spp goal of therapy from less than 140 to less than 130 and this recommendation focused on the cut point at which there is likely to be benefit from antihypertensive drug therapy but many individuals classified as low risk based on their ascvd risk score still have subclinical atherosclerosis based on their coronary calcium scores and may not be truly at low risk so is there an association between spp within the normal range as currently defined and ascvd in persons without traditional risk factors so this study was conducted in 1400 adults with 14 years of follow up and you can see the results here that these deciles of blood pressure going from left to right 90 99 100 109 and so on up to 129 all within the normal or slightly elevated range are associated with step wise
